description.narrative: Objectives: The project aims to promote a green economy model and inclusive development by supporting the Chè dây (Ampelopsis cantoniensis) production cooperative group in Song Vang Commune to develop a sustainable value chain. It seeks to enhance women’s production and business capacity, establish a legally recognized cooperative, and enable Co Tu ethnic minority women to gradually participate and benefit from the local value chain. Key activities include: - Conducting a baseline and endline survey toassess the cooperative group’s capacity and income changes of Co Tu women before and after joining the model. - Organizing one training course on business planning, group management, and marketing, followed by six months of coaching to develop a Chè dâybusiness plan. - Conducting communication activities to mobilize Co Tu women’s participation in the Chè dây production model. - Supporting at least 30 women to plant Chè dây to expand the raw material area and 30 households (possibly overlapping) with fertilizer support to enhance productivity and quality. - Compiling and publishing a technical manual on green-oriented Chè dây production and conducting one training course on green economy and sustainable cultivation practices. - Establishing a community-based monitoring mechanism to ensure compliance with the green production process. - Organizing two meetings to develop and approve cooperative/group operational regulations. - Providing one tea-roasting machine and one drying machine, installed at the Quyet Thang village community hall, to improve product quality and hygiene. - Supporting the establishment of a Chè dây cooperative upgraded from the current cooperative group and forming a four-member core operational team responsible for coordination, communication, and monitoring. - Designing a brand identity and packaging, producing communication materials such as videos, photos, and product stories. - Supporting two sales channels (one online, one offline) and conducting local promotion activities through fairs, banners, and exhibitions. - Organizing one networking workshop to connect cooperatives, enterprises, and local authorities, promoting market linkages and fair-trade practices. Project Area and Duration: The project will be implemented in Song Vang Commune, Dong Giang District, Da Nang City, over 18 months (December 2025 – May 2027). Project Beneficiaries: The project will benefit approximately 70 people, with ≥70% women and ≥50% Co Tu ethnic minority, all residing in Song Vang Commune. Direct beneficiaries (45 people): - 22 cooperative member households (≈30 people, 70% women) supported to strengthen capacity, commercialize products, and expand markets. - At least 15 of 25 mobilized Co Tu women directly involved in production, processing, packaging, and marketing. - 30 households supported with new cultivation packages (seedlings, organic fertilizer, trellising materials) and 30 others with fertilizer support. - A four-member core team trained and supported with allowances tocoordinate and sustain the model. Indirect beneficiaries (25 people): - 10 Co Tu women engaged in awareness-raising and knowledge sharing. - 10 local laborers benefiting from expanded cultivation and processing. - Local enterprises and communication units involved in packaging and product promotion. - Five commune officers (Women’s Union, Farmers’ Association, CPC,...) improving their capacity to manage green livelihood models.
